content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after a recent spike or correction.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum or volatility.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then fails to correct downward quickly — model lags in recognizing the peak and overreacts later.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, underestimating sustained upward trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggests model lacks persistence in trend continuation.
- Model fails to capture the “tail risk” of sudden price drops after a prolonged rise — underestimates downside volatility in late horizon.
- When true prices show a strong upward trend, model’s forecast lags behind by 1–3 days, then gradually catches up — suggests delayed reaction to momentum.
- Model overreacts to short-term noise (e.g., minor price corrections) and underestimates the persistence of long-term trends.
